# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

S5 Wrap up the compound format option for ms: document it in the README and round out its tests so it is ready for review. (Nov 4, 2:32 AM)
**Investigated**: The compound formatter from commit d57cff2 in src/index.ts, including fmtCompound's handling of negatives, zero values and sub-second values. The README's "Time Format Written-Out" section, where the compound example had been placed. The existing compound tests in src/format.test.ts.

**Learned**: fmtCompound floors the absolute value to whole seconds, so milliseconds are dropped, and it returns "0s" when no parts remain, which also drops the sign for sub-second negatives such as -500 and -999. Days are the largest unit, so 400 days renders as "400d". The earlier round-trip test was ineffective: ms('1h 30m') returns NaN because parse() rejects spaced multi-unit input, so the assertion always passed. It has been removed.

**Completed**: The README has a dedicated "Compound Format" section with examples and stated rules: space-separated parts, zero parts skipped, days as the largest unit, seconds as the smallest, a single leading minus for negatives, and compound taking precedence over long. src/format.test.ts gained tests for precedence over long, the compound: false path, rollover at each unit boundary, negative multi-unit values, fractional milliseconds, and throwing on NaN, Infinity and string input. The ineffective round-trip assertion was removed. The suite passes at 182 of 182 tests with 100% coverage, biome reports no issues and tsc --noEmit is clean. Nothing has been committed yet.

**Next Steps**: Waiting on the user's decision about whether to commit these changes. The open question is whether sub-second negatives such as -500 should keep a sign (for example "-0s" or "-500ms") instead of the current "0s".

**Notes**: The sign behaviour for sub-second negatives is now pinned by tests and documented in the README, so changing it means updating the tests and README together. The README placement under the written-out heading was corrected by moving the section.
